messages:
maya: Heads-up — enterprise customer reported streaming responses truncating mid-stream in Safari and then the client reconnects repeatedly. They say partial JSON arrives (valid prefix) but stream cuts and client opens a new EventSource that gets a 304 from our CDN.

sam: Got the customer repro link. They attached HAR and browser console: `EventSource` shows `ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING` and then reconnect. Customer says it only happens behind their CDN (Fastly) and only in Safari 16/17. Chrome works.

maya: Pasted their minimal repro: `new EventSource("https://api.redwood.example/streams/session?token=REDACTED")`. They use our polyfill as fallback.

lee: Interesting — 304 could be the culprit. If edge returns 304 with no body and strips Authorization on conditional requests, Safari's EventSource/HTTP stack can treat it as end-of-stream. Can you share the raw response headers when it truncates?

sam: From HAR (redacted):
```
GET /streams/session?token=...  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, s-maxage=60
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
X-Edge-Cache: HIT
...chunked stream data...\n(last chunk never received)\n
```
Then on reconnect:
```
GET /streams/session?token=...  HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, s-maxage=60
X-Edge-Cache: REVALIDATED
```
Edge didn't forward `Authorization` on the 304 request in their case (they are using header-based auth).

ana: (ops-bot) forwarded Fastly service config — looks like `cache_settings` are inserting `Vary: Authorization` removal and respecting revalidation without forwarding the header on conditional requests in their setup.

lee: That fits. Safari's EventSource keeps the original connection until it sees proper end (final chunk). If the edge revalidated and sent a 304 with no body and our origin never saw the conditional request (because auth header was stripped), the browser thinks stream ended mid-chunk. On reconnect the edge returns 304 (no body) so client never gets resumed stream fragments.

maya: Customer asked for concrete repro steps we can run against staging. I put together a curl-based repro that simulates conditional edge behavior: 
```
# open long-lived chunked response
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://staging.api.redwood/streams/keepalive" --no-buffer
# then simulate edge returning 304 on reconnect
curl -I -H "If-None-Match: \"xyz\"" "https://staging.api.redwood/streams/keepalive"
```

sam: I ran the `--no-buffer` curl. I can reproduce: after a few KBs the connection stops and we see `curl: (18) transfer closed with outstanding read data`.

lee: Proposed mitigations:
- Set SSE endpoints to `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` and ensure CDN bypass for `text/event-stream` paths.
- Ensure edge forwards auth headers for conditional requests or disable revalidation for SSE paths.
- Add a heartbeat comment chunk (e.g., `: keepalive\n\n`) every 15s to force browsers to treat connection open.

ana: I can add a rule to Fastly to `pass` for `path ~ ^/streams/` and to always forward `Authorization` and `If-None-Match` for that route. Will schedule a quick change in staging in 10m.

maya: Noted. Also flagged potential server-side improvement: make final chunk explicit (send `0\r\n` or close socket cleanly when session ends) and flush buffers. Lee, can runtime add extra chunk flush on session end?

lee: Yep — open ENG ticket ENG-12789 to add explicit final chunk and a periodic heartbeat in runtime for streaming responses. I'll own the PR.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: staging/fastly-config-pass-streams -> staged (id: fc-pass-2026-03-15).

ana: Change deployed to staging. I validated headers: `Cache-Control: no-store` and edge now forwards `Authorization` and `If-None-Match`.

sam: Re-tested against customer's HAR replay: Safari session stayed open, stream completed and final JSON arrived. No reconnect loop. Customer confirmed staging fix works for them as well (:white_check_mark:).

maya: Great. Next steps:
- Close customer ticket after confirming production rollout plan.
- ENG to land runtime fix (ENG-12789).
- Ops to rollout Fastly pass rule to prod during low traffic window.

lee: I'll submit the runtime PR today and mark as high priority for the release.

ana: I'll create a prod rollout ticket OPS-9123 and schedule a canary with monitoring on connection error rates.

maya: Thanks team. Adding summary for the customer: explain root cause (CDN revalidation + stripped auth + Safari EventSource handling of 304/no-body), mitigations (disable caching for SSE, forward auth headers, add heartbeat and explicit termination), and timeline for prod rollout.

ops-bot: ticket OPS-9123 created and assigned to ana.

maya: Closing thread once prod change is live. :thumbsup:
